overview: This bill, the Child Care Integrity Monitoring Act, requires the Department of Health and Human Services to do a full review every three years of how each state is running the Child Care and Development Block Grant program, the main federal program that gives states money to help low-income families pay for child care. Based on that review, the department must label a state "high risk" if it has many unresolved or repeated audit problems, keeps failing to carry out plans to fix problems, or repeatedly fails to follow its approved state plan. States labeled high risk would face extra monitoring, as decided by the department. As of April 6, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was placed on the House calendar.
for: Supporters say regular reviews and extra scrutiny for states with repeated problems help catch mismanagement and fraud before more money is lost.
against: Critics say added federal reviews create more paperwork for states and federal staff, and the bill leaves it largely up to the department what extra monitoring involves.
